title: Check yourself: Controls that fail closed, and a person before the irreversible

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: Scenario: Dana runs the refund flow of a claims assistant. The service that screens incoming requests stops answering, and the code must choose between two behaviours for a request that asks for a refund. Which one fits the design rules on this page?

options.text: Hold it and tell the caller that the check is unavailable
options.says: A refund is a high-consequence action and the screen is an input control, so the design holds.

options.text: Let the request pass and flag it for a person to look at tomorrow
options.says: Ruled out because "A screen that is down and lets a request through is the opening an attacker waits for".

options.text: Run the request once more through the model's own safety training
options.says: Ruled out because the layers "answer different attackers and different mistakes", and the model's own training is not the missing screen.

options.text: Let the request pass because the later approval step will catch it
options.says: Ruled out because "an output control cannot stop a tool call that already happened", and a later step does not repair a gap on an earlier layer.

origin.section: What a control does when it fails

questions.stem: Scenario: Ravi reviews a design in which a model must "always ask a person before closing an account", a rule written in the system prompt. What is the main weakness of that design?

options.text: The sentence is too short for the model to follow it reliably under load
options.says: Ruled out because the page grants that "the model usually follows it", so reliability of following is not the weakness.

options.text: The rule should sit in the user turn so that the model reads it last
options.says: Ruled out because the sentence stays "a request to the model and not a control" wherever it sits.

options.text: Nothing forces the step to happen, because an instruction only asks
options.says: A line in a prompt is a request and a control is a step the model cannot skip.

options.text: The sentence repeats a rule the platform already applies to every account
options.says: Ruled out because "Every control has a failure mode of its own, and the design must say it", and no platform rule is assumed to hold it.
